limitations: All eight lessons and all 88 questions read completely, including every option, answer index, explanation and worked example. Semantic review, direct calculation, targeted source checking and execution do not constitute exhaustive sentence-to-source mapping or formal correctness proofs.

230 logged substantive correction groups, including code-domain repairs, false proofs, incorrect trace cells, inconsistent explanations, cost-model corrections and unsupported empirical claims. Counts are groups of edits, not all factual sentences. Minor code-width formatting is not separately counted. Gap notes overlap correction groups.

All 35 lesson Python fences and all nine quiz Python fences executed by dsa-patterns-check.py with 298,314 passing assertions. Expression and template fragments received documented fixtures (bit indices/mask and add/remove/valid callbacks); quiz heap-push fragment used a synthetic node. Brute-force oracles covered every ternary array through length seven, signed subarrays, small strings, all window sizes, histogram rectangles, pair sums, prefix queries, randomized intervals and grids, median prefixes, k-way merge, XOR identities and all 88 answer indices.

Supplemental dsa-patterns-extra-check.py passed 5,542 assertions: signed longest-subarray prefix-max algorithm checked exhaustively, exact quiz arithmetic and examples, naive lazy-heap growth to 100 entries for window size three, Python two-run sort comparison counts, Java modulo widening modeled with exact integers, permission bits and complement results. Total 303,856 assertions. No Java/C/C++ compiler or Linux syscall execution is claimed; those language/platform statements were checked against specifications/documentation. No empirical timing benchmark was performed.

Eighteen retrieved primary/official/academic sources checked in relevant sections, not full documents. Crow 1984 original-paper mirrors failed; historical date/title and connection to summed-area tables were checked through the retrieved Viola-Jones primary paper including its references, not an independently read Crow original. The first Princeton lecture URL failed; the archived 2018 course copy was retrieved and scheduling/partitioning proofs read. Dijkstra EWD608 is a later related variant; EWD398 directly describes the original red/white/blue pebble problem and invariant.

Original Count-Min paper/archive retrieval failed; Apache implementation documentation directly confirms that the base sketch answers supplied-key estimates without listing heavy hitters. A turnkey sketch-plus-heap recipe was removed with an explicit gap because no candidate-recovery algorithm or error parameters were specified. The Apache page contains an unrelated contradictory error-direction sentence; this review relies only on its key-enumeration/API statement, not that sentence.

General numeric operation and hash-table assumptions are explicit where material. Python big integers, floating-point median precision, recursion-free finite-input examples, list allocation, output storage and hashing worst cases limit literal constant-time claims. Existing source-link reachability checks are inherited from docs/audit-links.json and are not semantic proof. Original plain diagram fences and shared diagram overrides were not edited.

Visible omissions explain absent universal runtime/feasibility figures, candidate failure prevalence, and underspecified approximate heavy-hitter recovery. Practical interview advice is framed as advice rather than population-wide fact or success guarantee. No low-confidence factual claim is intentionally retained as verified.
